audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for divorce debate, children, rich man, camel/needle, first-last reversal, third passion prediction, servant greatness, ransom language, and Bartimaeus.

verses.restored: Rising from there, he came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan; crowds gathered again to him, and as was his custom, he taught them again.

familiar.text: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judaea by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

modern.text: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.

original.text: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας ⸀καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Pharisees came and asked him whether it is lawful for a man to release his wife, testing him.

familiar.text: And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.

modern.text: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.

original.text: ⸀Καὶ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He answered, What did Moses command you?

familiar.text: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?

modern.text: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;

verses.restored: They said, Moses permitted writing a document of release and releasing her.

familiar.text: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.

modern.text: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· ⸂Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς⸃ βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this command.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, For the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.

modern.text: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.

original.text: ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην·

verses.restored: But from the beginning of creation, male and female he made them.

familiar.text: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.

modern.text: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’

original.text: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν ⸀αὐτούς·

verses.restored: Because of this a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,

familiar.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

modern.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,

original.text: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα ⸂καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ⸃,

verses.restored: and the two will become one flesh; so they are no longer two but one flesh.

familiar.text: And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.

modern.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

original.text: καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν· ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ·

verses.restored: Therefore what the Divine joined together, let a human not separate.

familiar.text: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

modern.text: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

original.text: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.

verses.restored: In the house the disciples questioned him again about this.

familiar.text: And in the house his disciples asked him again of the same matter.

modern.text: When they were back inside the house, the disciples asked Jesus about this matter.

original.text: Καὶ ⸂εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸂περὶ τούτου⸃ ⸀ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He said to them, Whoever releases his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.

modern.text: So He told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ⸀ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπʼ αὐτήν,

verses.restored: And if she releases her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.

familiar.text: And if a woman shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.

modern.text: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.” Jesus Blesses the Children (Matthew 19:13–15; Luke 18:15–17)

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν ⸂αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον⸃ μοιχᾶται.

verses.restored: They were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

familiar.text: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.

modern.text: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

original.text: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα ⸂αὐτῶν ἅψηται⸃· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ⸂ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς⸃.

verses.restored: Seeing this, Jesus was indignant and said, Allow the children to come to me; do not hinder them, for of such is the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

modern.text: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

original.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: whoever does not receive the reign of the Divine like a child will certainly not enter it.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.

verses.restored: Taking them in his arms, he blessed them, placing hands on them.

familiar.text: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.

modern.text: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them. The Rich Young Man (Matthew 19:16–30; Luke 18:18–30)

original.text: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ ⸂κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτά⸃.

verses.restored: As he was going out on the way, one ran up, knelt before him, and asked, Good Teacher, what shall I do so that I may inherit age-long life?

familiar.text: And when he was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?

modern.text: As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up and knelt before Him. “Good Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

original.text: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except the Divine alone.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.

modern.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: You know the commands: Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.

familiar.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

modern.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’ ”

original.text: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ ⸂φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς⸃, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

verses.restored: He said to him, Teacher, all these I have guarded from my youth.

familiar.text: And he answered and said unto him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth.

modern.text: “Teacher,” he replied, “all these I have kept from my youth.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἔφη αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου.

verses.restored: Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said, One thing you lack: go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.

familiar.text: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

modern.text: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me. ”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν ⸀σε ὑστερεῖ· ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς ⸀τοῖς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει ⸀μοι.

verses.restored: But he became gloomy at the word and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

familiar.text: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

modern.text: But the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

original.text: ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.

verses.restored: Looking around, Jesus said to his disciples, How difficult it is for those having wealth to enter the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

modern.text: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”

original.text: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται.

verses.restored: The disciples were amazed at his words. Jesus answered again, Children, how difficult it is to enter the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

modern.text: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus said to them again, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

original.text: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ⸀ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·

verses.restored: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

modern.text: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

original.text: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ ⸂τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς⸃ ῥαφίδος ⸀διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.

verses.restored: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, Then who is able to be saved?

familiar.text: And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved?

modern.text: They were even more astonished and said to one another, “Who then can be saved?”

original.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ⸀ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;

verses.restored: Looking at them, Jesus said, With humans it is impossible, but not with the Divine; for all things are possible with the Divine.

familiar.text: And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

modern.text: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”

original.text: ⸀ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλʼ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ ⸀δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: Peter began to say to him, Look, we have left everything and followed you.

familiar.text: Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.

modern.text: Peter began to say to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed You.”

original.text: Ἤρξατο ⸂λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος⸃ αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ⸀ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.

verses.restored: Jesus said, Amen, I say to you: there is no one who has left house, brothers, sisters, mother, father, children, or fields because of me and because of the good message,

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel’s,

modern.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel

original.text: ⸂ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ ⸂μητέρα ἢ πατέρα⸃ ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,

verses.restored: who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time: houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, with pressures, and in the coming age, age-long life.

familiar.text: But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.

modern.text: will fail to receive a hundredfold in the present age—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions—and in the age to come, eternal life.

original.text: ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ ⸀μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

verses.restored: But many first will be last, and the last first.

familiar.text: But many that are first shall be last; and the last first.

modern.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” The Third Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 20:17–19; Luke 18:31–34)

original.text: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ⸀οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.

verses.restored: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going before them. They were amazed, and those following were afraid. Taking the twelve again, he began to tell them the things about to happen to him.

familiar.text: And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen unto him,

modern.text: As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him:

original.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, ⸂οἱ δὲ⸃ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο. καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν

verses.restored: Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Humanity will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes; they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the nations.

familiar.text: Saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles:

modern.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles,

original.text: ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ ⸀τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν

verses.restored: They will mock him, spit on him, flog him, and kill him; and after three days he will rise.

familiar.text: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

modern.text: who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.” The Request of James and John (Matthew 20:20–28)

original.text: καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ⸂ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν⸃ καὶ ⸀ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ ⸂μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας⸃ ἀναστήσεται.

verses.restored: James and John, sons of Zebedee, came to him, saying, Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you.

familiar.text: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire.

modern.text: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”

original.text: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης ⸀οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες ⸀αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν ⸀σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.

verses.restored: He said to them, What do you want me to do for you?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you?

modern.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ⸀ποιήσω ὑμῖν;

verses.restored: They said, Give us that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.

familiar.text: They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory.

modern.text: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς ⸂σου ἐκ δεξιῶν⸃ καὶ εἷς ἐξ ⸀ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?

familiar.text: But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?

modern.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ⸀ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;

verses.restored: They said to him, We are able. Jesus said to them, The cup that I drink you will drink, and the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:

modern.text: “We can,” the brothers answered. “You will drink the cup that I drink,” Jesus said, “and you will be baptized with the baptism that I undergo.

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸀Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε,

verses.restored: But to sit at my right or left is not mine to give, except for those for whom it has been prepared.

familiar.text: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared.

modern.text: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”

original.text: τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ⸀ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλʼ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.

verses.restored: Hearing this, the ten began to be indignant about James and John.

familiar.text: And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John.

modern.text: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.

original.text: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.

verses.restored: Calling them, Jesus said to them, You know that those seeming to rule the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

familiar.text: But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.

modern.text: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

original.text: ⸂καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But it is not so among you. Whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant.

familiar.text: But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:

modern.text: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

original.text: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ⸀ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλʼ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ⸂μέγας γενέσθαι⸃ ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,

verses.restored: Whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.

familiar.text: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.

modern.text: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.

original.text: καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν θέλῃ ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι⸃ πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·

verses.restored: For even the Son of Humanity did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life/soul as a ransom for many.

familiar.text: For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

modern.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.” Jesus Heals Bartimaeus (Matthew 20:29–34; Luke 18:35–43)

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.

verses.restored: They came to Jericho. As he was going out from Jericho with his disciples and a sufficient crowd, Bartimaeus son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the way.

familiar.text: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side begging.

modern.text: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.

original.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ. καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ⸀ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος ⸀τυφλὸς ⸂προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν⸃.

verses.restored: Hearing that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me.

familiar.text: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.

modern.text: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ ⸀Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· ⸀Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.

verses.restored: Many rebuked him so that he would be silent, but he cried out much more, Son of David, have mercy on me.

familiar.text: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.

modern.text: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

original.text: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.

verses.restored: Jesus stood still and said, Call him. They called the blind man, saying, Take courage; rise, he calls you.

familiar.text: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

modern.text: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”

original.text: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· ⸂Φωνήσατε αὐτόν⸃. καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ⸀ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.

verses.restored: Throwing off his cloak, he sprang up and came to Jesus.

familiar.text: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.

modern.text: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ⸀ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, What do you want me to do for you? The blind man said, Rabbouni, that I may see again.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight.

modern.text: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν⸃· Τί ⸂σοι θέλεις ποιήσω⸃; ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Go; your trust has saved/healed you. Immediately he saw again and followed him on the way.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.

modern.text: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ὁ⸃ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει ⸀αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
